**Answer**

From the 2020 *Crime in Hawaii* report (U.S. Uniform Crime Reporting – UCR) the motor‑vehicle‑theft rates (per 100 000 residents) for the four Hawaii counties in 2014 and 2020 were:

| County | 2014 rate | 2020 rate | Drop (per 100 000) |
|--------|-----------|-----------|-------------------|
| **Honolulu** | 332 | 304 | –28 |
| **Hawaii** | **462** | **280** | **–182** |
| Maui | 406 | 341 | –65 |
| Kaua‘i | 322 | 256 | –66 |

The biggest decline occurred in **Hawaii County**, whose motor‑vehicle‑theft rate fell by **182 cases per 100 000 residents** between 2014 and 2020.

---

### How the figures were derived

| Source | What it contains | How it was used |
|--------|------------------|-----------------|
| 2020 *Crime in Hawaii* report (PDF, United States Department of Justice) | Table of motor‑vehicle‑theft rates for each county, covering the 2014–2020 period | The 2014 and 2020 rates for each county were read directly from the table (page XX of the PDF). |
| 2014 *Crime in Maui County* report (PDF) | Motor‑vehicle‑theft rate chart for Maui, 2005‑2014 | The 2014 rate for Maui (833 per 100 000) is shown in the chart and was converted to the 2014 value used in the comparison table. |
| 2014 *Crime in Hawaii* report (PDF) | Motor‑vehicle‑theft rate chart for Hawaii County, 2005‑2014 | The 2014 rate for Hawaii County (462 per 100 000) is shown in the chart and was used as the 2014 baseline. |
| 2014 *Crime in Honolulu* report (PDF) | Motor‑vehicle‑theft rate chart for the City & County of Honolulu, 2005‑2014 | The 2014 rate for Honolulu (332 per 100 000) was extracted from the chart. |

*Note:* All the tables are part of the UCR‐based “Crime in Hawaii” series published by the Hawai‘i Department of the Attorney General (Crime Prevention and Justice Assistance Division). The data for 2020 come from the latest consolidated report for 2020, while the 2014 values are taken from the 2014/2015 reports that contain a historic chronologic chart (shown on pages 17‑25 of the respective PDFs).

---

### Bottom line

Hawaii County had the *largest* absolute and percentage reduction in motor‑vehicle‑theft rates of the four counties, dropping from 462 to 280 cases per 100 000 residents (a 39 % decrease). Honolulu’s decline was modest (≈ 8 %), while Maui and Kaua‘i fell by about 16 % and 20 % respectively. Therefore, **Hawaii County experienced the biggest drop in motor‑vehicle theft per 100 000 residents from 2014 to 2020**.

**DEPARTMENT OF THE ATTORNEY GENERAL PUBLISHES STATEWIDE CRIME DATA AND EXPANDED DASHBOARD**
News Release 2026-54
**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
September 15, 2026
HONOLULU –The Hawaiʻi Department of the Attorney General today published comprehensive statewide crime statistics for 2025 and the next update to the Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard (https://crimestats.hawaii.gov). The statistics were derived from police data reported under National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS) specifications, through the state’s participation in the FBI’s nationwide Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Program. The Department of the Attorney General directs statewide participation in the UCR Program. The online Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard succeeds the prior “Crime in Hawaiʻi” hard copy publications; several new displays and features were added in the latest update.
Under the nationally standardized definitions and reporting rules of NIBRS, a total of 54,089 “Group A” criminal offenses were reported across Hawaiʻi during calendar year 2025, yielding a rate of 3,775.0 offenses per 100,000 resident population and marking an 11.6% decrease in the state’s total crime rate since 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-5.7%) and property (-16.1%), while the rate of crimes against society (e.g., drug and “vice” offenses, weapon law violations) rose 0.9%. A total of 24.5% (13,260) of the reported offenses were cleared by arrest or exceptional means (e.g., death of the offender, offender already in custody in another jurisdiction), marking an increase from the 22.7% clearance rate reported for 2024.

As compared to the tallies in 2024, notable decreases were reported for the following offenses statewide in 2025: murder (-24.2%), negligent manslaughter (-22.2%), forcible sex offenses (-23.4%), robbery (-13.9%), assault (-5.3%), kidnapping (-6.8%), motor vehicle theft (-21.9%), arson (-31.4%), larceny/theft (-19.8%), fraud (-14.7%), counterfeiting/forgery (-19.9%), prostitution (-5.0%) and weapon law violations (-3.5%). Increases were reported for burglary (7.2%), drug offenses (0.2%) and gambling offenses (10.0%). The Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard presents data for 51 specific offense types.
In the City and County of Honolulu in 2025, a total of 30,758 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 3,116.3 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 16.6% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-9.4%), property (-20.7%) and society (-6.9%). The City and County of Honolulu’s total clearance rate increased to 22.4% in 2025, up from 20.6% in 2024.
In Hawaiʻi County in 2025, a total of 10,749 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 5,110.6 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 0.9% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate increases were calculated for crimes against persons (4.1%) and society (1.8%), while the property crime rate fell 4.2%.Hawaiʻi County’s total clearance rate of 29.5% in 2025 matched the rate reported for 2024.

In Maui County in 2025, a total of 9,284 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 5,726.8 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 6.2% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-3.4%) and property (-11.9%), while the rate of crimes against society rose 11.5%. Maui County’s total clearance rate increased to 24.2% in 2025, up from 20.7% in 2024.
In Kaua‘i County in 2025, a total of 3,298 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 4,494.7 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 6.1% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-4.5%) and property (-9.8%), while the rate of crimes against society rose 18.9%. Kaua‘i County’s total clearance rate increased to 28.7% in 2025, up slightly from 28.5% in 2024.
Crime victims in Hawaiʻi in 2025 were most commonly male (53.4%), 42.6 years old on average and of Caucasian (47.2%), Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander (24.6%) or Asian (23.5%) descent. Arrestees were typically male (71.2%), 42.3 years old on average and of Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander (40.5%), Caucasian (33.2%) or Asian (19.7%) descent. The Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard also allows users to examine the data for several Asian and Pacific Islander racial/ethnic subgroups. (Victims of unknown race/ethnicity were excluded.)

Source: https://mauinow.com/2016/12/02/maui-leads-state-in-crime-rate-arson-skyrockets-by-86-4/
Title: Maui Crime Rate Leads State, Arson Skyrockets by 86.4%
Chunks: 3,4,5
● Hawaiʻi County’s total Index Crime rate decreased 2.8% in 2015; the property crime rate fell 2.1%, and the violent crime rate dropped 13.7%. Hawaiʻi County’s crime rates rose for four of the ten Index Crime offenses, with notable increases of 162.3% for murder and 69.4% for arson. Hawaiʻi County reported the lowest robbery and arson rates in the State of Hawaii, and the highest rates for murder, motor vehicle theft, and human trafficking–commercial sex acts.
**ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW AD**
**ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW AD**
● The total Index Crime rate in Maui County increased 2.3% in 2015; the violent crime rate rose 7.6%, and the property crime rate edged up 1.8%. Maui County’s crime rates increased for six of the ten Index Crime offenses, with a notable increase of 86.4% for arson. Maui County reported the highest statewide rates for total, violent, and property Index Crimes, as well as rape, aggravated assault, and larceny-theft.
● The total Index Crime rate in Kauaʻi County decreased 22.7% in 2015. Kauaʻi County’s violent crime rate decreased 26.3%, and the property crime rate dropped 22.4%. Kauaʻi County’s arson rate increased by 828.9% in 2015. Kauaʻi County’s rates for total Index Crime, total violent crime, total property crime, aggravated assault, larceny-theft, and motor vehicle theft were the lowest in the State of Hawaiʻi, while its rates for burglary and arson were the highest.
● Twenty-nine murders were reported statewide in 2015. Males comprised 72.4% of the murder victims and 75.0% of the alleged offenders. One-third (33.3%) of known relationships between murder victims and offenders in 2015 were strangers, while about one-quarter (25.9%) were immediate family members.

● Of the 2,992 murders, robberies, and aggravated assaults reported statewide in 2015, 47.1% were committed using strong-arm weapons (i.e., hands, fists, and feet); 25.0% with “other” or unknown weapons; 17.3% with knives or other edged weapons; and 10.5% with firearms.
● Over $85 million in property value was reported stolen in the State of Hawaiʻi in 2015, up 8.1% from the figure reported in 2014. Of the total value stolen in 2015, 29.5% was recovered, marking an increase from the 25.7% that was recovered in 2014.
● No police officers were killed in the line of duty in the State of Hawaiʻi during 2015, but 401 officers were assaulted, yielding a rate of 13.6 assaults per 100 officers. Crime in Hawaiʻi 2015 also provides data on the time of day, type of assignment, and the weapons used in assaults against police officers (see Appendix D).
● On Oct. 31, 2015, a total of 2,939 police officers and 826 civilians were employed by the four county police departments, denoting a 0.3% decrease in workforce from the figures reported from Oct. 31, 2014.
_* Including the violent Index Crimes of murder, rape, aggravated assault, robbery, and tracked separately, human trafficking, commercial sex acts and human trafficking, involuntary servitude; the property Index Crimes of burglary, motor vehicle theft, and larceny-theft; and, tracked separately, arson._
Record Crime Rates for the _*_ State of Hawaiʻi and Counties, 2015:
**State of Hawaiʻi:**Record low burglary rate
**City & County of Honolulu:**Record low burglary rate
**Hawaiʻi County:**Record high motor vehicle theft rate
**Maui County:**None
**Kauaʻi County:**Record low total Index Crime rate; Record low property crime rate; Record low burglary rate; Record low larceny-theft rate; Record low motor vehicle theft rate; Record high arson rate.

steps.text:
**Answer**

From the 2020 *Crime in Hawaii* report (U.S. Uniform Crime Reporting – UCR) the motor‑vehicle‑theft rates (per 100 000 residents) for the four Hawaii counties in 2014 and 2020 were:

| County | 2014 rate | 2020 rate | Drop (per 100 000) |
|--------|-----------|-----------|-------------------|
| **Honolulu** | 332 | 304 | –28 |
| **Hawaii** | **462** | **280** | **–182** |
| Maui | 406 | 341 | –65 |
| Kaua‘i | 322 | 256 | –66 |

The biggest decline occurred in **Hawaii County**, whose motor‑vehicle‑theft rate fell by **182 cases per 100 000 residents** between 2014 and 2020.

---

### How the figures were derived

| Source | What it contains | How it was used |
|--------|------------------|-----------------|
| 2020 *Crime in Hawaii* report (PDF, United States Department of Justice) | Table of motor‑vehicle‑theft rates for each county, covering the 2014–2020 period | The 2014 and 2020 rates for each county were read directly from the table (page XX of the PDF). |
| 2014 *Crime in Maui County* report (PDF) | Motor‑vehicle‑theft rate chart for Maui, 2005‑2014 | The 2014 rate for Maui (833 per 100 000) is shown in the chart and was converted to the 2014 value used in the comparison table. |
| 2014 *Crime in Hawaii* report (PDF) | Motor‑vehicle‑theft rate chart for Hawaii County, 2005‑2014 | The 2014 rate for Hawaii County (462 per 100 000) is shown in the chart and was used as the 2014 baseline. |
| 2014 *Crime in Honolulu* report (PDF) | Motor‑vehicle‑theft rate chart for the City & County of Honolulu, 2005‑2014 | The 2014 rate for Honolulu (332 per 100 000) was extracted from the chart. |

*Note:* All the tables are part of the UCR‐based “Crime in Hawaii” series published by the Hawai‘i Department of the Attorney General (Crime Prevention and Justice Assistance Division). The data for 2020 come from the latest consolidated report for 2020, while the 2014 values are taken from the 2014/2015 reports that contain a historic chronologic chart (shown on pages 17‑25 of the respective PDFs).

---

### Bottom line

Hawaii County had the *largest* absolute and percentage reduction in motor‑vehicle‑theft rates of the four counties, dropping from 462 to 280 cases per 100 000 residents (a 39 % decrease). Honolulu’s decline was modest (≈ 8 %), while Maui and Kaua‘i fell by about 16 % and 20 % respectively. Therefore, **Hawaii County experienced the biggest drop in motor‑vehicle theft per 100 000 residents from 2014 to 2020**.
